points.quote: An application such as `examples/browser` lists the extensions it wants as plain npm dependencies. ... `theia build`, from `@theia/cli` and `dev-packages/application-manager`, then bundles the frontend.
A Theia extension is an ordinary npm package that declares a `theiaExtensions` array in its `package.json`. Each entry names a module for each side

Each entry names a module for each side, for example `"frontend": "lib/browser/editor-frontend-module"` and `"backend": "lib/node/editor-backend-module"`. ... `src/browser` is the frontend. `src/node` is the backend.
Those modules are InversifyJS `ContainerModule`s. They bind services and contributions such as `CommandContribution`, `MenuContribution` and `FrontendApplicationContribution`.
`src/browser` is the frontend. `src/node` is the backend. `src/common` is shared code. `src/electron-browser` and `src/electron-main` are the Electron renderer and main processes.
It also has a `theia` section in its `package.json` for application properties such as the target (browser or Electron).

`frontend-generator.ts` writes a frontend entry ... `backend-generator.ts` does the same for the backend modules. `bundler-generator.ts` writes the esbuild configuration (`esbuild.mjs`). ... `theia start` runs the generated backend, which loads the backend modules and serves the bundled frontend. In this repo, `npm run start:browser` does this and serves on localhost:3000.
